_comment: Hand-built positions for the CDCE eval correctness tests required by
plan.md §6.3 ('Hand-built positions with exact expected term values').
Each FEN is a static legal position, not necessarily reachable from the
startpos by legal play -- that's fine for a unit test.
'expected' values are computed from the CdceParams::default() set (plan 6.2 pseudocode: N=420 R=330 Q=950; not the 'standard' set):
ONE_WAY_WEIGHT:   N=12  B=6   R=6   Q=3   P=4   K=0
Fork_Bonus:       40 (flat, not phase-scaled -- §6.2 lists no phase column)
Rook activity:    off_home_rank=25 (mg only), relative_rank3=20 (mg only),
integer division truncating toward zero (Rust i32 '/').
phase:            0..=24, weights N=1 B=1 R=2 Q=4 per piece, both sides.
Each position lists only the term(s) it's built to test. Other eval terms
(mobility, king safety, pawn structure, untested rook-activity bonuses)
may still be non-zero on these boards; they are out of scope for the
listed 'expected' entries unless explicitly called out in 'notes'.

positions.name: One-way knight-on-rook
positions.description: White knight e5 attacks black rook g6 (e5->g6 is a legal knight move). The rook on g6 attacks along rank 6 and file g, neither of which includes e5, so it cannot attack back: one-way.

expected.notes: Knight attacks exactly one enemy piece, so no fork bonus. Verify eval(white) reflects +39 from this term specifically (isolate by comparing against the same position with the rook removed).

positions.name: Mutual rook-on-rook (contributes 0)
positions.description: White rook d1 and black rook d8 face each other on the open d-file with nothing between (d2-d7 empty); both are on their own home rank. Each attacks the other, so the one-way condition (!att[t].has(a)) fails both ways.

expected.notes: Mutual sliders of the same type are always mutual per the §6.2 geometry note, so this term contributes exactly 0 net. Both rooks are on their home rank (no off-home-rank confound) and not on relative rank 3, but the d-file IS open for both, so rook_activity.file_open (+25 both phases) legitimately fires for both rooks independently -- that's a separate term, not part of this check.

positions.name: Pawn attacking a rook
positions.description: White pawn c4 attacks d5 (one of its two diagonal capture squares), occupied by a black rook. The rook on d5 attacks along rank 5 and file d, neither of which includes c4: one-way.

positions.name: Royal fork (knight forks king + queen)
positions.description: White knight e6 attacks both d8 (black king) and g7 (black queen) simultaneously -- a classic royal fork. FORK_TARGETS = {N, R, Q, K} includes both, so the fork bonus fires. Black is in check and to move.

white: OW[N][Q] = 12 * 950 / 100 = 114 (Ne6 -> Qg7; queen g7 cannot reach e6: |Δfile|=2, |Δrank|=1, not a line/diagonal)
OW[N][K] = 12 * 0 / 100 = 0 (Ne6 -> Kd8; king material value is 0 per §6.1, so this pair contributes 0 regardless of one-way-ness)

expected.notes: This position exercises both the fork term and the one-way term on the same knight, which is realistic (forks are usually also one-way attacks).

positions.name: Fork of two bishops (no fork bonus)
positions.description: White knight d5 attacks both c7 and e7, occupied by black bishops. Bishops are NOT in FORK_TARGETS = {N,R,Q,K} (the deliberate deviation from the pseudocode's VALUE-based target selection, §6.2), so no fork bonus despite attacking two pieces.

knight_forks.white: 0 (bishops excluded from FORK_TARGETS, even though count of attacked enemy pieces is 2)

one_way_attacks.white: OW[N][B] * 2 = (12 * 330 / 100) * 2 = 39 * 2 = 78 (Nd5 -> Bc7 and Nd5 -> Be7, neither bishop attacks d5 back: |Δfile|=1,|Δrank|=2 for both, not diagonal)

expected.notes: This is the key regression test for the FORK_TARGETS deviation: fork bonus must stay 0 here even though one-way attacks correctly fire twice.

positions.name: Open vs semi-open file -- open-file half
positions.description: White rook d1 on a d-file with no pawns of either color. Rook is on its home rank (rank 1) and not on relative rank 3, and is the only rook, so no other rook-activity term fires.

expected.rook_activity: file_open bonus = 25, both phases (PhasedScore(25, 25)); all other rook-activity conditions false

positions.name: Open vs semi-open file -- semi-open-file half
positions.description: Same as open_vs_semi_open_file_open, but with a black pawn added on d7. White has no pawn on the d-file, black does: semi-open for White.

expected.rook_activity: file_semi_open bonus = 12, both phases (PhasedScore(12, 12)); file_open must NOT also fire

positions.notes: Compare directly against open_vs_semi_open_file_open: the only board difference is the d7 pawn, and the only eval difference should be 25 -> 12 on this term (everything else identical).

positions.name: Rook lift on relative rank 3 -- full phase
positions.description: Standard starting material (phase = 24, the maximum) except White's a1 rook has been lifted to a3 (relative rank 3 for White); a1 is empty, castling rights adjusted to drop White's queenside right. The a-file is blocked by the a2/a7 pawns on both sides (no open/semi-open-file confound).

positions.name: Rook lift on relative rank 3 -- (near-)zero phase
positions.description: Same rook-on-a3 / a-file-blocked-by-pawns setup as rook_lift_rank3_full_phase, but every other N/B/R/Q piece is stripped from the board. Phase cannot be literally 0 while the tested rook is on the board -- a rook alone contributes phase weight R=2 -- so this is the minimum achievable phase (2/24) with the rook present, used as the 'zero phase' endpoint.

rook_activity.realized: (45*phase + 0*(24-phase)) / 24 = (45*2)/24 = 3.75 -> 3 (Rust integer division truncates toward zero; use the engine's actual tapering/rounding to confirm whether this lands on 3 or 4)

expected.notes: Contrast with rook_lift_rank3_full_phase: same mg-only raw bonus (45), but the realized (phase-tapered) score collapses from 45 to ~3-4 as phase goes from 24 to its practical minimum. This is the test that verifies the mg-only taper actually multiplies by phase instead of being a flat bonus.
